en: A block and tackle pulley system using four supporting rope segments allows you to lift a heavy object with only one fourth of its weight in force.
Geckos can climb smooth glass because millions of microscopic hairs on their feet create molecular attraction called van der Waals forces.
Because Earth bulges at the equator, a person weighs slightly less there than at the North or South Poles.
If you cut a permanent bar magnet in half, you do not get isolated poles, but two smaller complete magnets.
A single bolt of lightning heats the surrounding air to 30,000 degrees Celsius, making it five times hotter than the sun's surface.
Light travels about 25 percent slower through liquid water than it does through the empty vacuum of outer space.
Sound waves travel about fifteen times faster through solid steel than they do through the air in our classrooms.
Sweating cools your body because the phase change of liquid water turning into gas absorbs excess heat energy from your skin.
At the very top of a roller coaster, a cart possesses maximum gravitational potential energy before converting it into kinetic energy.
A standard doorknob operates as a wheel and axle simple machine, allowing a small rotational force to easily turn the internal latch.
A skydiver reaches terminal velocity when the upward force of air resistance exactly equals the downward pull of gravity.
Unlike permanent magnets, electromagnets only generate a magnetic field when an electrical current is actively flowing through their wire coils.
